prize_parts.citation: for the development of small molecules that harness the ubiquitin-proteasome system to induce targeted protein degradation, from heterobifunctional degraders to the cereblon mechanism of molecular glues

statement.case_for: After the first round I keep targeted protein degradation as my preferred configuration. It is the only shortlisted achievement that is a new design principle in chemistry (a small molecule that recruits an E3 ligase to a target, so that the cell destroys it catalytically) and that has visibly changed what chemists and clinicians can do: proteins without a conventional binding pocket are now addressable. The principle is reproduced across many independent academic and industrial laboratories, the ternary-complex chemistry is being measured quantitatively, and glue-class medicines already in clinical use are now explained by it. The chair asked whether one sentence can cover both strands. I think it can: the shared achievement is induced proximity to the ubiquitin-proteasome system as a chemical strategy, with Crews and Deshaies supplying the heterobifunctional concept and Handa supplying the cereblon mechanism that unified thalidomide-class glues with that logic. That same sentence is what justifies Handa over Ciulli as third name. Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work are an optimisation of a platform whose concept already existed, whereas the cereblon discovery changed the conceptual picture of an entire drug class.
statement.case_against: No heterobifunctional degrader is yet approved, so the clinical argument for PROTACs still rests on late-stage trials and on glue-class drugs whose mechanism was explained retrospectively, and I cannot confirm trial status from the materials I am allowed to read. A three-name limit also excludes Sakamoto, Ciulli, Gray, Ito and Kim, and a critic can fairly say that a combined citation stitches two strands that were developed separately. If the committee will not accept one sentence for both strands, my case weakens and B011 or B035 become the more defensible choices on maturity and attribution.

responses.point: Linke prefers B046 (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen), calling phase separation a clear physical principle that has reached hundreds of laboratories, while acknowledging that which in-cell condensates are truly phase-separated and functional is unsettled.
responses.response: I take the physical clarity seriously, and the in vitro framework of valency and saturation concentration is persuasive. But the committee would have to choose between crediting the in vitro thermodynamics, which is secure but not obviously a chemical discovery in the Nobel sense, and crediting the organization of living cells, which is the claim Linke himself calls unsettled. A citation can only be as strong as its weaker half. Until the field shows which condensates are functionally essential and can be manipulated deliberately, I cannot write a sentence about changed capabilities that I would defend, so I remain unmoved, and B046 stays outside my alternatives.

responses.point: Somfai prefers B035 (Buchwald and Hartwig) as the clearest case of a new reaction that became routine, with clean attribution, but worries that it is less novel conceptually than B010 or B011 and is close to the 2010 coupling prize.
responses.response: This is the strongest challenge to my position on maturity and attribution. Buchwald and Hartwig is the cleanest name set on the list, and I accept that C-N bond formation is chemically distinct from the C-C couplings of 2010, with Kosugi's precedent handled by a carefully worded citation. I agree with Somfai's own point that B035 is the less conceptually novel of the two. My preference for B010 depends on valuing a new principle with reach into medicine over a refinement, even a transformative one, of an existing catalytic logic. If B010 cannot gather support because of the missing PROTAC approval, B035 is the configuration I would move to, and I now list it as an alternative.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers B011 with Balasubramanian and Klenerman only, as reversible-terminator sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry, ranks B010 as an alternative but somewhat early, and judges B011 free of maturity risk.
responses.response: His narrowing to two names answers my first-round worry about attribution across platforms, and it makes B011 more defensible than I thought: a prize for reversible terminators and clustered sequencing-by-synthesis is a chemical citation, and the omission of Rothberg is at least principled. I keep B011 as an alternative. Where I still disagree is on timing as a differentiator, since the concept behind degraders has been validated for roughly 25 years in independent laboratories and a glue-class mechanism is already explained. I also still doubt that B011 will avoid the Medicine-or-technology objection raised in the summary, which is why it remains second for me.

responses.point: Chabes shares the Crews, Deshaies, Handa trio and prefers a citation that explicitly names induced-proximity degraders and the cereblon mechanism of glues, while asking whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name.
responses.response: We converge on names, and I have borrowed his wording, since it answers the chair's question directly by naming both strands. Where I would push back is the risk he accepts, that a bundled citation is open to criticism as stitching. I would resolve it by tying both strands to one explicitly stated principle (induced proximity to the ubiquitin-proteasome machinery) and by stating plainly that Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Ito and Kim are not credited because the prize is limited to three names, which does not make their work less real. I also share his request for an expert report on trial and approval status before the vote, because neither of us can confirm it from the materials here.

uncertainties: Whether one citation can honestly cover heterobifunctional degraders and cereblon-based glues, or the committee will insist that they are two achievements.

Whether the absence of an approved heterobifunctional PROTAC is a decisive timing objection for colleagues who weight completed clinical record; the status of late-stage trials and glue-class approvals is recalled, not verified.
Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name; I would not block Ciulli if that gathered a majority.
Priority details for Sakamoto, Kim and Ito relative to Crews, Deshaies and Handa are recalled from memory and not verified.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal ground has changed since round 1. My postdoc mentors (Molly Stevens, Freddy Boey) and my Linkoping colleagues are not credited on any shortlisted ballot. My work on peptide-nanoparticle biosensing overlaps in field with chemical biology generally, but not with any credited candidate, and I have no personal or institutional tie to Crews, Deshaies, Handa or the alternatives.
